recipe_context.name: dissulfurimicrobium_hydrothermale_medium
recipe_context.notes: Source: JCM | Link: https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1030

preparation_steps.description: Mix components, except sulfur, bring to a boil and cool down under a CO2 (100%) gas stream. While gassing, add the following components to the medium:

Bubble CO2 for 3 - 4 min and check pH to be 6.5 - 6.8. Readjust pH to the range, if necessary. Then, suspend ferrihydrite (see below) in the medium and dispense the suspension into culture vessels (e.g., 10 ml in Hungate tubes) under a CO2 gas stream. Add appropriate amount of sulfur (powder). Seal the culture vessels with butyl rubber stoppers and autoclave at 105C for 1 hr.

Ferrihydrite: Slowly titrate 320 ml of FeCl3 x 6H2O solution (60.0 g/L) with 10% (w/v) NaOH to pH 7.0-7.5 with agitation on a magnetic stirrer (approximately 80-100 ml NaOH solution). Remove ferrihydrite into a container, cover with water and store at room temperature overnight. Remove supernatant after centrifugation at 2000 rpm for 5 min.

recipe_context.name: vr_salts_b
recipe_context.notes: Rogosa 1969 defines VR salts solution B as a one-liter stock made from magnesium, calcium, iron, zinc, manganese, cobalt, vanadium, molybdate, and copper salts, HCl, nitrilotriacetic acid, distilled water, and 10 N NaOH to dissolve the NTA. KOMODO imported only the NaOH pH-buffer note for this submedium.

preparation_steps.description: Dissolve the magnesium, calcium, iron, zinc, manganese, cobalt, vanadium, molybdate, and copper salts in about 700 ml water by applying heat and adding 2 ml HCl.
Separately add nitrilotriacetic acid to 300 ml distilled water with stirring and add 10 N NaOH until the pH tends to stabilize at 7.0 to 7.4 and the NTA dissolves.
Slowly add the NTA solution to the stirred mixed-salts solution until the stock becomes fairly clear.
Adjust the volume of VR salts solution B to 1 liter.
Filter VR salts solution B through paper.
Refrigerate the filtered VR salts solution B stock.

preparation_steps.description: Dissolve ingredients except carbonate, trimethylamine, DTT, cysteine, and vitamins. Sparge the medium with an 80% N2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture for at least 30-45 minutes to make it anoxic. Then, dispense it under the same gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials and autoclave. Add trimethylamine, DTT, cysteine, and vitamins from sterile anoxic stock solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas and carbonate from a sterile anoxic stock solution prepared under 80% N2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture. Solutions of DTT and vitamins should be sterilized by filtration. Adjust the pH of the complete medium to 7.4 with an anoxic, sterile solution of 5% w/v Na2CO3, if necessary.
Note: A white precipitate that forms after autoclaving of the mineral base will dissolve again after storage at room temperature for 2 - 3 days.

preparation_steps.description: Mix components, except sulfur, bring to a boil and cool down under a CO2 (100%) gas stream. While gassing, add the following components to the medium:

Bubble CO2 for 3 - 4 min and check pH to be 6.5 - 6.8. Readjust pH to the range, if necessary. Then, suspend ferrihydrite (see below) in the medium and dispense the suspension into culture vessels (e.g., 10 ml in Hungate tubes) under a CO2 gas stream. Add appropriate amount of sulfur (powder). Seal the culture vessels with butyl rubber stoppers and autoclave at 105C for 1 hr.

Ferrihydrite: Slowly titrate 320 ml of FeCl3 x 6H2O solution (60.0 g/L) with 10% (w/v) NaOH to pH 7.0-7.5 with agitation on a magnetic stirrer (approximately 80-100 ml NaOH solution). Remove ferrihydrite into a container, cover with water and store at room temperature overnight. Remove supernatant after centrifugation at 2000 rpm for 5 min.

preparation_steps.description: Prepare the bottom layer from FeS solution, Modified Wolfe's solution, and Agar, Noble.
Prepare the top layer from Modified Wolfe's solution and Trace minerals.
Autoclave both layer solutions at 121 degrees C for 15 min.
Shortly after autoclaving, pipette the bottom layer into each culture vessel, typically 5 ml in a 60 ml glass vial with a cut pipette tip.
Cool the bottom layer for at least 30 min to solidify.
After cooling the top layer, add filter-sterilized Trace vitamins and 8% NaHCO3 solution per liter.
Add the top layer solution at five to six times the bottom-layer volume to culture vessels containing solidified bottom layer.
Cap culture vessels with silicone rubber stoppers and replace the gas phase with an N2-CO2 (4:1, v/v) gas mixture.
For storage, cap vessels with butyl rubber stoppers instead of silicone rubber stoppers and keep the vessels anoxic.

solutions.notes: 10x basal salts stock solution; 100.0 ml added per liter before autoclaving.
1.0 L trace element stock solution; 1.0 ml added per liter before autoclaving.

preparation_steps.description: Mix 0.2 g NaNO2, 2.0 g MES, 100 ml Stock solution, and 1.0 ml Trace element solution in 900 ml distilled water.
Adjust pH to 6.3.
Autoclave at 121 C for 15 min.

curation_history.notes: Direct import from JCM GRMD=1503. Structured MES-buffered pH 6.3 autotrophic Nitrobacter recipe and its 2 stock solutions with CHEBI/MediaIngredientMech grounding.
Assigned stable identifier: CultureMech:015920

preparation_steps.description: Mix ingredients except vitamin solution, sulfur, and Na2S·9H2O.
Adjust pH to 7.0.
Autoclave under a N2 atmosphere.
Filter-sterilize the vitamin solution.
Sterilize sulfur by autoclaving for 60 minutes at 105 C on each of 3 successive days.
Neutralize Na2S·9H2O as a 5% solution and autoclave under N2.
Before inoculation, aseptically and anaerobically add vitamin, sulfur, and Na2S·9H2O.

recipe_context.name: ammonia_oxidizing_bacteria_medium
recipe_context.notes: Source: JCM | Link: https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1483 | Multi-table JCM recipe: Solution A (800 ml) and Solution B (200 ml) are autoclaved separately and combined with Solution C (0.5 ml), Solution D (1.0 ml), and 0.05% (w/v) Phenol red solution (2.5 ml) to yield ~1004 ml final medium.

composition.notes: 1 drop per 100 ml stock

solutions.notes: Filter-sterilized 100 ml stock solution; 0.5 ml added per liter after combining Solutions A and B.
Filter-sterilized 1.0 L trace element stock solution; 1.0 ml added per liter.
Filter-sterilized 0.05% (w/v) phenol red stock (pH 7.0); 2.5 ml added per liter.

preparation_steps.description: Prepare Solution A ((NH4)2SO4 2.0 g, NaCl 0.5 g, MgSO4·7H2O 0.05 g, CaCl2·2H2O 0.02 g in 800 ml distilled water) and Solution B (KH2PO4 0.5 g in 200 ml distilled water) and autoclave separately.
Prepare Solution C (Fe-EDTA solution), Solution D (trace element solution), and 0.05% (w/v) phenol red solution (adjusted to pH 7.0 with NaOH) and sterilize each by filtration.
After cooling, combine Solution A and Solution B and aseptically add 0.5 ml Solution C, 1.0 ml Solution D, and 2.5 ml 0.05% phenol red solution.

Adjust pH to 7.8 with filter-sterilized 10% (w/v) NaHCO3 solution. During cultivation, re-adjust pH to ~7.8 with sterile 10% NaHCO3 solution whenever the medium turns yellow-orange due to nitrite production.

curation_history.notes: Direct import from JCM GRMD=1483. Manually curated multi-table JCM recipe (Solutions A, B, C, D and Phenol red indicator stock) that import_jcm_grmd.py skipped in SKIP_GRMDS.

Phase-2 CAUTION: this parent record is explicitly ANAEROBIC (DSMZ 88a / TOGO M2670; Na2S reducing agent + N2 gas phase). Every literature strain retrieved (Willard et al. 2024) was cultivated on AEROBIC low-sulfate Brock's salts (DSM-88) in vented serum bottles, using NH4Cl instead of (NH4)2SO4 and without Na2S/N2. These strains are therefore scoped to an aerobic Brock's-salts MediaVariant and their evidence explanations explicitly state growth is NOT verified on the anaerobic parent. S. acidocaldarius MW001, Saccharolobus solfataricus P2, and Sulfuracidifex tepidarius DSM 104736 were EXCLUDED entirely because phase-2 judged their medium a distinct record, not a variant. Sulfodiicoccus acidiphilus HS-1T is the only strain with a genuinely anaerobic (MBSY + Na2S + H2/CO2) formulation and is the closest to the parent, though its basal recipe is also cited transitively. Constituent composition researched from product specification.

Original nominal final volume is1001ml, while listed liquid inputs total1001.5ml. Use1.001 L for the ten main mass rates, rounded to six significant digits, not measured precision or assumed additive volume. Preserve exact stock batch inputs without inventing final stock denominators.

Preserve preparation stages: anoxic main preparation, separate clarified-fluid procedure, mineral-stock titration and fatty-acid-stock titration. Existing preparation steps remain source-scoped; storage filling fractions are not medium concentrations.

Complete inspected source rows define this reconstruction. Archive false LB expansions, flattened quantities and placeholders in append-only history. Preserve earlier supported evidence exactly; unrelated chemical annotations are not recertified.

preparation_steps.description: Dissolve ingredients (except bicarbonate, vitamins, cysteine and sulfide) and sparge medium for 30 - 45 min with 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture to make it anoxic. Add and dissolve bicarbonate and adjust pH to 6.8, then distribute under same gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials and autoclave. After sterilization add cysteine and sulfide from sterile anoxic stock solutions autoclaved under 100% N2 gas atmosphere. Vitamins are prepared under 100% N2 gas atmosphere and sterilized by filtration. Adjust pH of complete medium to 6.5. For incubation use sterile 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture at two atmospheres of pressure.

Rumen fluid from cow or sheep (obtained from fistulated animals or abattoir refuse) is filtered through muslin, autoclaved at 121°C for 15 min and then centrifuged at 27,000 g for 20 min. The supernatant is made anoxic by sparging with 100% N2 gas for 15 min, dispensed under same gas atmosphere into anoxic serum vials to 30% of volume and then stored frozen at -20°C.
First dissolve nitrilotriacetic acid and adjust pH to 6.5 with KOH, then add minerals. Adjust final to pH 7.0 with KOH.
Adjust pH to 7.5 with concentrated NaOH.

Clarified rumen fluid (from medium 1310)
Rumen fluid from cow or sheep (obtained from fistulated animals or abattoir refuse) is
filtered through muslin, autoclaved at 121°C for 15 min and then centrifuged at 27,000 g
for 20 min. The supernatant is made anoxic by sparging with 100% N2 gas for 15 min,
dispensed under same gas atmosphere into anoxic serum vials to 30% of volume and then
stored frozen at -20°C.

Dissolve ingredients (except bicarbonate, vitamins, cysteine and sulfide) and sparge
medium for 30 - 45 min with 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture to make it anoxic. Add and
dissolve bicarbonate and adjust pH to 6.8, then distribute under same gas atmosphere into
anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials and autoclave. After sterilization add cysteine
and sulfide from sterile anoxic stock solutions autoclaved under 100% N2 gas atmosphere.
Vitamins are prepared under 100% N2 gas atmosphere and sterilized by filtration. Adjust
pH of complete medium to 6.5. For incubation use sterile 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas
mixture at two atmospheres of pressure.




Clarified rumen fluid (from medium 1310)
Rumen fluid from cow or sheep (obtained from fistulated animals or abattoir refuse) is
filtered through muslin, autoclaved at 121°C for 15 min and then centrifuged at 27,000 g
for 20 min. The supernatant is made anoxic by sparging with 100% N2 gas for 15 min,
dispensed under same gas atmosphere into anoxic serum vials to 30% of volume and then
stored frozen at -20°C.
